behavior: With no repo-local hook and a .pre-commit-config.yaml present, the dispatcher routes the stage to `pre-commit hook-impl --hook-type <stage>` with the config passed explicitly.
A non-zero exit from pre-commit propagates out of the dispatcher, so the operation is actually blocked.
The pre-push ref list on stdin reaches pre-commit unmodified, so it scans the commits being pushed rather than the staged file set.
An executable repo-local hook still wins and pre-commit is not additionally invoked, so no gate runs twice.
A missing config or a missing pre-commit binary is a clean exit 0, so the machine-wide dispatcher never breaks git in unrelated repos.
The fallback is stage-generic: pre-commit and commit-msg route correctly and forward their own arguments.
The GUARD-001 memory-sink guard still runs first and can still veto a commit.
